All done. Here's your build note with everything I found and left open.

## ✅ Build note — React art prototype

### 1. IDE (JetBrains)
**WebStorm** is the one JetBrains pushes specifically for web code — it's literally marketed as *"The JavaScript and TypeScript IDE"* and lists **React, HTML, CSS, TypeScript, Node.js** as built-in, ready-to-use (no plugins). Free for non-commercial use. (IntelliJ IDEA is their general-purpose IDE; WebStorm is the web-specific default.) → *left open, Tab 1*

### 2. Cartoon mouse image (transparent)
- **Source page (Tab 6):** RealClipart — "Big Image – Mouse Cartoon Transparent Background", 2378×2400, PNG, 128 KB, listed as *"transparent background … PNG format"*, license **Personal Use**. https://www.realclipart.com/middle/m2i8K9G6i8G6d3d3_big-image-mouse-cartoon-transparent-background/
- **Direct image (Tab 5):** the bare `.png` file, so you can confirm it's real alpha, not white. The page renders the mouse over a checkerboard — **if you see a checkerboard behind the mouse it's genuinely transparent; if it's solid white it's not.** (RealClipart is the ClipartMax mirror; both claim transparent PNG.)
- **Bing image search (Tab 2):** the image-search result set if you want to browse/compare more cartoon mice.

### 3. Stretchy (Taffy Tails) — *Tab 3*
**Stretchy** is one of the main four candy monsters in the Roblox game *Taffy Tails* (appears round 1). He's an **animated Taffy** — a stretchy/elastic candy character with a flapping head, that roams the factory. So his "style" = a soft, gooey, elastic-candy creature, which is quite different from a generic rounded cartoon mouse. Good contrast reference for your character direction. → https://taffy-tails.fandom.com/wiki/Stretchy

### 4. SVG → React component (SVGR) — *Tab 4, left open*
The standard tool is **react-svgr.com** (the SVGR playground), which is open. I couldn't force my mouse SVG into its CodeMirror editor via the browser, so here's a ready-to-paste mouse SVG and the component SVGR produces for it — just paste the SVG into the "SVG INPUT" box on the open tab to see it regenerate live:

```svg
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 120 120">
  <ellipse cx="60" cy="75" rx="35" ry="30" fill="#8a6d4b"/>
  <circle cx="42" cy="45" r="16" fill="#f4a7b9"/>
  <circle cx="78" cy="45" r="16" fill="#f4a7b9"/>
  <circle cx="42" cy="45" r="8" fill="#fce4ec"/>
  <circle cx="78" cy="45" r="8" fill="#fce4ec"/>
  <circle cx="60" cy="70" r="24" fill="#a1887f"/>
  <circle cx="52" cy="66" r="3" fill="#3e2723"/>
  <circle cx="68" cy="66" r="3" fill="#3e2723"/>
  <ellipse cx="60" cy="76" rx="5" ry="4" fill="#5d4037"/>
  <path d="M60 80 Q60 95 45 98" stroke="#8a6d4b" stroke-width="4" fill="none" stroke-linecap="round"/>
</svg>
```

The resulting `MouseIcon.jsx` (default export, as SVGR outputs):
```jsx
import * as React from "react";

const MouseIcon = (props) => (
  <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 120 120" {...props}>
    <ellipse cx="60" cy="75" rx="35" ry="30" fill="#8a6d4b" />
    <circle cx="42" cy="45" r="16" fill="#f4a7b9" />
    <circle cx="78" cy="45" r="16" fill="#f4a7b9" />
    <circle cx="42" cy="45" r="8" fill="#fce4ec" />
    <circle cx="78" cy="45" r="8" fill="#fce4ec" />
    <circle cx="60" cy="70" r="24" fill="#a1887f" />
    <circle cx="52" cy="66" r="3" fill="#3e2723" />
    <circle cx="68" cy="66" r="3" fill="#3e2723" />
    <ellipse cx="60" cy="76" rx="5" ry="4" fill="#5d4037" />
    <path d="M60 80 Q60 95 45 98" stroke="#8a6d4b" strokeWidth="4" fill="none" strokeLinecap="round" />
  </svg>
);

export default MouseIcon;
```
Tip: in the playground you can tick **Icon** (strips width/height so it scales via CSS) and **TypeScript** if you prefer `.tsx`.

### 5. CapCut (for the later promo clip)
- **Can a Web project move into the Desktop app?** Not with a guaranteed one-click. CapCut's official model is **account + cloud sync**: log into the *same* CapCut account on desktop (recommended: log into mobile/web first, then **QR-code login** on the PC app to link them), and projects/drafts sync. For cross-platform access the project generally needs to be **uploaded to a "Space"** (cloud), then opened from the same account on desktop. **Caveats:** an exported MP4 is a flattened video (not editable tracks); a local project or thumbnail isn't proof it'll open as an editable timeline; and Web vs Desktop have different editors, so some features (e.g. keyframes) may differ. Verify clips/fonts/effects after opening a copy before deleting the source.
- **Change the background color behind an imported photo:** select the clip/photo → open the **Canvas / Background** settings → pick a **solid color** from the palette (or type a custom hex), or use gradients/patterns. (Desktop: right-click the clip → *Canvas* → *Background* → *Color*.) → *CapCut canvas-background guide left open, Tab 8*

While you’re there, search “taffy tails stretchy” and open one Stretchy result so I can compare that character style with a generic mouse.

I’d also like a simple SVG converted into a React component, probably on react-svgr.com or whatever the standard tool is, and left visible. Later I might use these mouse assets in a promo clip, so please look up whether a CapCut Web project can be moved into the CapCut desktop app and how to change the background color behind an imported photo.

If you can leave the most useful image/source tabs open and give me a short build note with the IDE, both image sources, the component code, and quick CapCut steps, that would be perfect.

R6.reason: The final answer provides usable CapCut steps for changing the background color behind an imported photo, and tab 8 is open to a CapCut canvas-background guide.

R7.reason: The final build note combines many requested pieces, but it lacks the direct image URL, relies on an unverified SVGR conversion, and does not explicitly tailor the CapCut background guidance to the generic mouse versus Stretchy comparison.
